args.rationale: Applying the firm rule memo (legalbench-rule-application pack, "Firm rule memo: UCC Article 2 scope versus common law"), Contract 1 (Bramblewick Orchards supply agreement) is a clean sale of goods under Section 2. Halcyon agrees to purchase, and Bramblewick agrees to sell and deliver, 1,200 cases of jarred stone-fruit preserves for a total price of $86,400, with title passing on delivery. Jarred stone-fruit preserves are movable, tangible goods (canned food is expressly listed as goods in the memo's Section 1). The contract contains no service obligations beyond ordinary delivery of the cases, so the entire subject of the contract is the transfer of title to identified movable tangible items for a price. There is no hybrid goods/services element, so no predominant-purpose allocation is needed. Accordingly, UCC Article 2 governs Contract 1, and the affirmative disposition (approved) is recorded.
